title: NCSO 01 - Exam map and weak spots
description: Study point: Review the NCSO exam structure and list 3 weak areas to prioritize. Note that national/provincial exams are closed-book and typically require 75% to pass.

title: NCSO 02 - Health and safety program basics
description: Study point: Name the core pieces of a construction health and safety program: policy, roles, hazard control, training, inspections, investigations, emergency response, records, and review.

title: NCSO 03 - Internal responsibility system
description: Study point: Explain how employers, supervisors, workers, contractors, and safety personnel each share responsibility for site safety. Make one jobsite example for each role.

title: NCSO 04 - Legislation and due diligence
description: Study point: Review employer/supervisor/worker legal duties and the idea of due diligence. Write the proof you would need to show reasonable care was taken.

title: NCSO 05 - Worker rights and responsibilities
description: Study point: Memorize the rights to know, participate, and refuse unsafe work. Add what the worker must do when reporting a hazard or refusing work.

title: NCSO 06 - Hazard identification methods
description: Study point: Compare formal inspections, FLHA/JHA, worker observations, incident trends, and pre-job planning as ways to find hazards before work starts.

title: NCSO 07 - Risk assessment ranking
description: Study point: Practice rating a hazard by severity and likelihood. Pick one construction hazard and decide if it is low, medium, high, or critical risk.

title: NCSO 08 - Hierarchy of controls
description: Study point: Put controls in order: elimination, substitution, engineering, administrative, PPE. Give one example for falls, silica/dust, and moving equipment.

title: NCSO 09 - Safe work practices and procedures
description: Study point: Know the difference between a safe work practice and a safe job procedure. Draft a 4-step procedure for a routine site task.

title: NCSO 10 - FLHA/JHA walkthrough
description: Study point: Take one job, break it into steps, identify hazards for each step, and choose controls. Focus on controls that are specific and measurable.

title: NCSO 11 - Site inspections
description: Study point: Review what a good inspection records: location, hazard, risk, corrective action, responsible person, due date, and follow-up evidence.

title: NCSO 12 - Incident investigation steps
description: Study point: Memorize the investigation flow: secure scene, care for people, report, gather facts, interview, analyze causes, recommend controls, follow up.

title: NCSO 13 - Root cause vs direct cause
description: Study point: Sort examples into immediate causes, basic/root causes, and system weaknesses. Avoid blaming workers without identifying failed controls.

title: NCSO 14 - Corrective actions
description: Study point: Turn one incident finding into a SMART corrective action. Include owner, due date, verification method, and how recurrence will be prevented.

title: NCSO 15 - WHMIS and SDS
description: Study point: Review WHMIS pictograms, labels, and SDS sections. Pick one product and find hazards, PPE, first aid, storage, and spill response.

title: NCSO 16 - PPE selection and limits
description: Study point: Match PPE to hazards, then state the limitations. Include hard hats, eye/face, hearing, respiratory, gloves, footwear, and fall protection.

title: NCSO 17 - Occupational hygiene basics
description: Study point: Review exposure routes, monitoring, OEL/TLV concepts, and controls for noise, silica/dust, fumes, heat/cold stress, and ergonomics.

title: NCSO 18 - Emergency preparedness and first aid
description: Study point: Identify what an emergency plan must cover: contacts, alarms, evacuation, muster, rescue limits, first aid, drills, and communication.

title: NCSO 19 - Training and orientations
description: Study point: Outline what belongs in a site orientation and when refresher training is needed. Include competency checks and training records.

title: NCSO 20 - Toolbox talks and communication
description: Study point: Prepare a 2-minute toolbox talk on one hazard. Include the hazard, why it matters, controls, worker input, and sign-off documentation.

title: NCSO 21 - Preventive maintenance
description: Study point: Review how maintenance reduces incidents. Compare pre-use inspections, scheduled maintenance, defects/out-of-service tags, and repair records.

title: NCSO 22 - Auditing and COR evidence
description: Study point: Review audit evidence types: documents, interviews, and observations. Connect each evidence type to one health and safety program element.

title: NCSO 23 - Records and safety statistics
description: Study point: Review why records matter. Define leading vs lagging indicators and calculate a simple incident rate or inspection completion percentage.

title: NCSO 24 - Practice questions and recall
description: Study point: Do 10 practice questions or flashcards. For each miss, write the correct answer, why it is correct, and the topic to revisit.

title: Morning Serenity Check
description: Al-Anon detachment; Family & Friends self-management; RCA showing up calmly. What is mine to handle today, and what belongs to someone else? Write one sentence for each.

title: Three-Column Boundary Note
description: Al-Anon boundaries; Family & Friends coping plan; RCA relationship safety. Fill columns: I can do / I cannot do / I will do if needed.

title: One Kind, Clear Request
description: RCA communication; Family & Friends positive communication; Al-Anon own-your-part. Practice: I feel ___ when ___. I would like ___. Name behavior, not character.

title: Relationship Weather Report
description: RCA coupleship awareness; Al-Anon inventory; Family & Friends emotional regulation. Rate serenity, honesty, resentment, willingness, and connection from 1-5 without fixing immediately.

title: Pause Before Helping
description: Al-Anon detachment; Family & Friends CRAFT; RCA loving boundaries. Before advising or rescuing, ask: Is this help, control, fear, or love? Choose one small action or no action.

title: Coupleship Inventory Bite
description: RCA relationship inventory; Al-Anon personal inventory; Family & Friends self-awareness. Finish: protected myself / protected the relationship / avoided saying honestly.

title: CRAFT-Style Positive Reinforcement
description: Family & Friends reinforcement; RCA appreciation; Al-Anon focus on healthy behavior. Notice one healthy behavior and offer one brief, sincere appreciation for that specific behavior.

title: Resentment To Need
description: Al-Anon resentment work; Family & Friends values; RCA honest sharing. Translate one resentment: I resent ___ because I need or value ___.

title: Mini Detachment Practice
description: Al-Anon letting go; Family & Friends distress tolerance; RCA reducing pressure. Write: I release my claim on ___ for the next 24 hours.

title: Repair Without Over-Owning
description: RCA repair; Al-Anon own-your-side; Family & Friends clear communication. Write: I am sorry for my part in ___. Next time I will ___.

title: Meeting Reflection
description: All three programs; daily carry-forward. After a meeting, write one phrase to carry today and one action before bed.

title: Values-Based Choice
description: Family & Friends values; Al-Anon serenity; RCA loving conduct. Ask what serenity, dignity, and love look like in the next 10 minutes; choose one behavior.

title: Couple Recovery Question
description: RCA shared recovery; Family & Friends collaboration; Al-Anon realistic expectations. If safe, ask: What is one small thing we can do today that supports recovery for both of us?

title: Support Contact
description: Al-Anon fellowship; RCA sponsor-couple idea; Family & Friends support network. Send one short text or make one brief support call telling the truth simply.

title: Evening Release
description: Al-Anon turning over; RCA daily repair; Family & Friends coping and reset. Write three lines: showed up by / turning over / tomorrow I can begin again by.

title: One Story, Many Voices 01 - Decide format
description: Choose the final format: booklet, study guide, class handout, video series, discussion group, or website. Pick the intended audience.

title: One Story, Many Voices 02 - Create outline
description: Build the main outline covering scripture/canon, Genesis, Moses, Jesus/Isa, why traditions differ, and next sources.

title: One Story, Many Voices 03 - Break into sessions
description: Turn the concept into 8-10 study sessions from canon through creation, Abraham/Ibrahim, Moses/Musa, Mary/Maryam, Jesus/Isa, and tradition differences.

title: One Story, Many Voices 04 - Story comparison charts
description: Make a comparison chart for each major story with columns for Ethiopian Orthodox, Roman Catholic, Baptist/Protestant, and Islam.

title: One Story, Many Voices 05 - Primary readings
description: Choose short primary-source readings from Genesis, Exodus, Gospel passages, Quran passages, 1 Enoch, and Jubilees.

title: One Story, Many Voices 06 - Check claims and sources
description: Verify dates, canon counts, council references, translation claims, and citations. Separate faith teaching from scholarly interpretation.

title: One Story, Many Voices 07 - Simplify language
description: Rewrite dense scholarly paragraphs into clear discussion-friendly explanations and define key terms like canon, Septuagint, Masoretic Text, Hadith, Tafsir, and Miaphysite.

title: One Story, Many Voices 08 - Discussion questions
description: Add questions for each section: emphasis, surprise, source used, meaning change, and respectful comparison.

title: One Story, Many Voices 09 - Create handouts
description: Create handouts: canon comparison, timeline, glossary, and one chart per major story.

title: One Story, Many Voices 10 - Tone rules
description: Decide tone rules: scholarly, respectful, no tradition mocked or corrected, differences presented as meaningful.

title: One Story, Many Voices 11 - Introduction
description: Prepare a short introduction explaining that the goal is understanding, not debate, and each tradition should be read on its own terms.

title: One Story, Many Voices 12 - Final packet
description: Assemble outline, charts, readings, glossary, and discussion questions into one clean study packet with title page, table of contents, and recommended next readings.

description: Walk the house and empty every trash can into the outdoor bin, and put fresh bags in.

description: Strip the old sheets, put on a fresh set, and start a load of laundry with the dirty ones.

title: Clean mirrors and glass doors
description: Spray and wipe down mirrors and any glass doors so they're streak-free.

title: Assess physical safety
description: Is there risk of violence or escalation during separation? Contact a domestic abuse line even if it's 'just' emotional abuse — BPD rages count. Alberta: 780-482-5525 (Women's Emergency Accommodation Centre).

title: Secure important documents
description: Gather passports, birth certificates, SIN cards, and your own financial records. Move copies to a safe location outside the home — parent, trusted friend, safety deposit box, or scanned to a private cloud folder he doesn't have access to.

title: Change passwords on key accounts
description: Change passwords on email, banking, phone plan, and any accounts he has access to. Do this in sequence — email first, then banking, then anything linked to email.

title: Create a private email account
description: Set up a private email account he is unaware of — for legal and financial correspondence only.

title: Open a personal bank account
description: Open a bank account in your name only if you don't already have one. Begin routing your own income here before separation is announced, if legally and safely possible.

title: Create a family safety plan with the kids
description: Create a calm, age-appropriate safety plan with Oliver and Logan. Who do they call? Where do they go? What's the code word for 'come get me'? Frame it as a family plan, not an emergency.

title: Allow yourself to grieve
description: Grieve not just the marriage, but the version of him you hoped he would become. You are not leaving who he is — you are letting go of who you believed he could be. Those are two different losses.
questions: What am I grieving that never actually existed? What am I grieving that was real?
worksheetText: Sit with this without trying to resolve it. Grief is not a problem to solve.

title: Name the patterns you absorbed
description: Identify survival habits from the relationship: walking on eggshells, hypervigilance, managing his moods, minimizing your own needs. These kept you safe. They will need to be gently unlearned.
questions: Which of these patterns show up in my life outside of him? Which ones are hardest to let go of?
worksheetText: List 3 survival habits. Next to each, write: 'This kept me safe by ___. I no longer need it because ___.' Be gentle.

title: Sit with the question: Why did I stay?
description: Reflect on the stories you told yourself to stay — 'He'll change,' 'It's the BPD talking,' 'The kids need their dad.' Not to shame yourself, but to understand and release them.
questions: What did I tell myself to stay? Which of those stories were true? Which were hope?
worksheetText: Write out the stories without judgment. Then write: 'I now know that ___.' No shame. Just truth.

title: Work through responsibility for his sobriety
description: Process the question of whether you feel responsible for his sobriety or emotional wellbeing post-separation. You are not. His drinking is not your fault, your failure, or your burden to carry forward. BPD does not change this.
questions: Where do I still feel responsible for him? What would I tell a friend in my position?
worksheetText: Write the sentence: 'His sobriety is not mine to carry.' Write it until it feels true, not just logical.

title: Acknowledge the ambivalence
description: Loving someone and needing to leave them are not opposites. You can grieve him and still know this is right. You can miss him and still walk out the door.
questions: What am I still holding love for? Can I hold that tenderly while still moving forward?

title: Identify your support people
description: Who can you call at 11pm? Who won't say 'I told you so'? You need at least one person who can hold you without advice, and one who can help you make practical decisions.
worksheetText: Write down 3 names. Next to each, write what role they play. Then reach out to at least one this week.

title: Begin or return to individual therapy
description: Find a therapist experienced in trauma, codependency, or personality disordered relationships. Al-Anon is also deeply valuable alongside therapy, not instead of it.

title: Resist the closure conversation
description: Resist the urge to explain yourself to him or get him to understand why you're leaving. BPD and active alcoholism rarely allow for the closure conversation you deserve. You may need to find closure without his participation.
questions: What am I still hoping he will say or do? Can I give that to myself instead?

title: Journal: The moment I knew
description: Write about the moment you knew — not when you decided, but when you knew. Private journal entry, no rules.
worksheetText: Prompt: 'The moment I stopped believing it would get better was...' Let yourself be honest. No one is reading this but you.

title: Journal: Letter to Oliver and Logan
description: Write a letter to your kids — not to give them, but to articulate why you're doing this for them. Keep it. Read it on hard days.
worksheetText: Prompt: 'I'm choosing this because I want you to know what a home can feel like when...'

title: Journal: Name every fear
description: Write about what you are afraid will happen — name every fear without filtering. Being alone. Money. His reaction. The kids. Then write next to each: 'And if that happens, I will...'
worksheetText: Prompt: 'I am afraid that...' List them all. Then answer each one with a plan.

title: Journal: The woman on the other side
description: Write about the woman you want to become on the other side of this. Not goals. Not a list. Just how she feels in her body, in her home, in her mornings.
worksheetText: Prompt: 'In three years, she feels...' Write without stopping for 10 minutes.

title: Journal: The things you never said
description: Write the things you never said — and never will. Let them exist on paper. The anger. The grief. The gratitude. The rage. Write it and don't send it. Some things are for God, not for him.
worksheetText: Write a letter you will never send. Say everything. Then decide what to do with the page.

title: Tell Oliver and Logan together
description: Tell the kids as a united front if possible, with a simple, calm, consistent message. 'Mom and Dad have decided to live in separate homes. This is a grown-up decision. You are loved by both of us and none of this is your fault.'

title: Prepare the answer to 'Why?'
description: Have an honest, age-appropriate answer ready for when the kids ask why. You don't have to say everything. 'Dad has some really hard problems that he is working on, and right now our family works better in two homes' is enough.
worksheetText: Write out your answer and say it out loud a few times before the conversation.

title: Teach the kids: it was never their job
description: Help Oliver and Logan understand they are not responsible for their dad's feelings or behaviour. Name it gently: 'It was never your job to keep Dad calm. That was never a kid's job.'

title: Tell the kids what stays the same
description: Name everything that isn't changing before you name what is — school, friends, activities, their rooms, their routines. Kids in transition need anchors.

title: Create a 'feelings are okay' framework
description: Oliver and Logan may feel sad, angry, relieved, guilty, or all of these at once. Tell them: 'However you feel is the right way to feel. You don't have to feel one thing.' Consider a feelings chart or a quiet corner at home.

title: Watch for parentification
description: Watch for signs that Oliver or Logan are trying to take care of you or manage your emotions. Gently redirect: 'I'm the parent. I'm okay. Your job is just to be a kid right now.' Get them into a child therapist if this is significant.

title: Talk with the kids about time with their dad
description: Be honest about what's predictable and what isn't during their time with their dad. 'Dad sometimes has a hard time managing his feelings, and that's not your fault and not something you can fix' is okay to say.

title: Look into Alateen for the kids
description: Al-Anon has a kids program called Alateen — peer support from other children of alcoholics. Oliver and Logan don't have to be alone in understanding what life with an alcoholic parent was like.

title: Commit to not speaking negatively about their dad
description: Establish this rule for yourself: never speak negatively about their dad in front of Oliver or Logan, even when it is hard. They are half of him. Save your processing for your people, your therapist, your journal.

title: Consult a family law lawyer
description: Book an initial consultation with a family law lawyer familiar with high-conflict separation, addictions, and mental health. Many offer free 30-minute sessions. Edmonton: Community Legal Centre (780-702-1725) for lower-income options.

links.label: Law Society of Alberta Lawyer Referral

title: Record your legal separation date
description: In Alberta, you must be separated for one year before a divorce is granted (unless abuse). The date of separation matters legally — note it and write it down. You can live in the same home and be considered legally separated if you document it.
worksheetText: Write down the date you consider separation to have begun and why. Keep this in a secure place.

title: Start a private incident log
description: Keep a private log of dates, times, behaviours, and any witnesses — especially relevant for custody concerns. What he said, what happened, what the kids witnessed. Store in your private email or secure cloud folder.

title: Gather financial disclosure documents
description: Both parties must fully disclose finances in Alberta. Gather: tax returns (3 years), pay stubs, bank statements, RRSP/pension statements, property tax notices. Get ahead of this.

title: Understand matrimonial property division
description: In Alberta, property acquired during marriage is generally shared equally. Exceptions include gifts and inheritances. Know the value of: the home, vehicles, savings, debts, pensions, and any business interests.

title: Draft a Separation Agreement
description: Work with your lawyer to draft a Separation Agreement covering: division of property and debt, spousal support (if applicable), child support (Federal Child Support Guidelines), and parenting/custody arrangements.

title: Create a Parenting Plan
description: Write a Parenting Plan covering: regular schedule, holiday schedule, how decisions about school/medical/religion are made, and how you communicate (ideally in writing). Apps like OurFamilyWizard help with high-conflict co-parenting.

title: Consider supervised visitation
description: If Oliver and Logan are at risk during his care, you can request supervised access through the court. Document incidents that support this. Your lawyer will advise on what threshold is required.

title: File for child support
description: Child support is a legal right, not optional, and is calculated on income using the Federal Child Support Guidelines. Alberta's Maintenance Enforcement Program (MEP) can automatically collect and disburse payments.

title: Update Will and beneficiary designations
description: Remove him from your Will and update life insurance and RRSP beneficiaries. Do not skip this — it has major consequences if something happens to you before the divorce is finalized.

title: Update Personal Directive and Power of Attorney
description: Until divorce is finalized, he may retain legal decision-making authority in a medical emergency if you don't update your Personal Directive and Enduring Power of Attorney to remove him.

title: Determine the housing plan
description: Determine who stays in the home or if it will be sold. In Alberta, both spouses have equal right to remain in the matrimonial home until a court order or agreement says otherwise.

title: Build a single-income budget
description: Build a realistic budget for one-income living, including child support incoming. Factor in: housing, utilities, food, vehicle, kids' activities, insurance, and debt payments.

title: Notify kids' schools of the separation
description: Update Oliver and Logan's schools with emergency contacts and pickup permissions. Clarify who has pick-up authority during different custody periods. Provide written instruction if there is any risk he may show up impaired.

title: Update addresses and contact info
description: Once you have a permanent address, update: CRA (Service Canada), employer, bank, health insurance, Oliver and Logan's schools, Alberta Health.

title: Untangle shared subscriptions and accounts
description: Review shared subscriptions, streaming accounts, phone plans, and any other digital access. Separate what you can when it is safe to do so.

title: Attend Al-Anon
description: Attend Al-Anon — not because you did anything wrong, but because you need people who understand this specific kind of pain. Fort Saskatchewan area meetings available through Al-Anon Canada. You don't have to share. You can just sit.

title: Read: Codependent No More
description: Read 'Codependent No More' by Melody Beattie — one of the most honest books about loving an addict. Also consider: 'Stop Walking on Eggshells' (Mason & Kreger) for BPD relationships, and 'The Body Keeps the Score' when you're ready.

title: Reclaim one thing that was yours before him
description: Reclaim one small thing that was yours before him — a hobby, a friendship, a piece of who you were. Not as a coping mechanism, but as an act of remembering that you existed before this marriage and you will exist after it.
questions: What did I love before I was trying to love him well?

title: Lean into FSCC — let the church be your support
description: Let Fort Saskatchewan Community Church be part of your support, not a source of shame. Divorce is not a spiritual failure. Protecting your children and yourself is faithful.

title: Give yourself permission to not have it figured out
description: You do not have to know who you are after this. You just have to put one foot in front of the other until the fog clears. That is enough.
worksheetText: Serenity Prayer: God grant me the serenity to accept the things I cannot change, courage to change the things I can, and wisdom to know the difference.
